Package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter

Class CsrfTokens

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter.CsrfTokens
Direct Known Subclasses:
CsrfTokens.PerSession
public abstract sealed class CsrfTokens extends Object permits CsrfTokens.PerSession (not exhaustive)
Where a CSRF synchronizer token comes from, and how it is masked for embedding and checked on the way back.

Two strategies are available:

  • perSession() — the default. The token is HMAC-SHA256(key, UTF-8(sessionId)), so every session has its own token and nothing is stored in the session. An attacker who can load the page in their own browser learns only their own token, never the victim's.
  • perProcess() / perProcess(SynchronizerToken) — one token for the whole process. It needs no session, but any visitor can read it, so in a multi-user application it adds little beyond the Origin check.
Masking

The value written into a page is never the token itself. Each embed gets a fresh 32-byte pad, and the published value is hex(pad || (pad XOR token)): 128 lower-case hex characters. The secret therefore never repeats across renders or across the several places one page embeds it, which defeats an HTML compression oracle (BREACH). That is all masking buys: anyone who sees the wire value can unmask it, so the token header must never be logged, and masking gives no protection to logs, proxies or the browser.

Verification

A presented value must be exactly 128 lower-case hex characters; anything else is refused before the secret is touched. It is then unmasked and compared with MessageDigest.isEqual(byte[], byte[]) against the expected 32 bytes. A request with no session is compared against the HMAC of a fixed placeholder id that no container can issue, so "no session" and "wrong token" do the same work and give the same answer.

Session ids

A per-session token changes whenever the session id changes, and this class never changes it. An application must call HttpServletRequest.changeSessionId() on login; otherwise a token seen before login stays valid after it.

Example:

// Default: one token per session, keyed by 32 fresh random bytes for this process. CsrfTokens tokens = CsrfTokens.perSession(); // A cluster: every node shares one CSPRNG-generated key, so any node accepts any node's token. CsrfTokens clustered = CsrfTokens.perSession().key(keyBytesFromSecretStore);

  • Method Details

    • perSession

      public static CsrfTokens.PerSession perSession()
      A per-session strategy keyed by 32 fresh random bytes.

      Each call returns a strategy with its own key, so tokens from two instances never cross-verify. Use CsrfTokens.PerSession.key(byte[]) to share one key across a cluster.

      Returns:
      A new per-session strategy.

    • perProcess

      public static CsrfTokens perProcess(SynchronizerToken token)
      A per-process strategy holding the given token.

      The token's value must be exactly 64 lower-case hex characters (32 bytes), which is what SynchronizerToken.generate() produces. Any other value is refused rather than stretched or hashed into shape: a passphrase is not a secret of the required strength, and quietly accepting one would hide that.

      Parameters:
      token - The process token. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      A new per-process strategy.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If token is null or its value is not 64 lower-case hex characters.
